title: Descent of canonical duality and Tor bounds for a degree-zero module
statement: Let Lambda be a commutative condensed ring, X a scheme, M a Lambda_X-module sheaf, and {U_i -> X} a pro-etale cover. Let a,b be integers. Suppose every M|U_i placed in degree zero is dualizable in the relative derived category and has Tor amplitude in [a,b], testing tensor against every module sheaf. Then the global canonical map M[0] tensor RHom(M[0],1) -> RHom(M[0],M[0]) is an isomorphism, and M[0] has Tor amplitude in [a,b]. All coefficients, inverse images and relative derived Hom are those of [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom].

proof.text: Apply condensed_dualizable_iff_proetale_cover to M[0]. Exact pullback commutes with singleFunctor, so each assumed local dual identifies with the required derived pullback. Global dualizability follows. Obtain the braided structure and swap the exact pairing to use MonoidalClosed.isIso_ihomUnitTensorToIhom. This makes the canonical global comparison invertible without detecting equality of maps locally.

source.place: Proof, global canonical duality comparison (steps 3, 4 and 7)

proof.text: For an arbitrary module sheaf G, let L=M[0] tensor G[0]. Derived pullback on a cover member is strong monoidal and commutes with singleFunctor, so its pullback of L is the local module tensor against the restriction of G. The local Tor bound makes each H^q of this object zero for q<a or b<q. Exact pullback commutes with homology. Apply joint conservativity to the degree-zero complex of H^q(L), then faithfulness of singleFunctor, to deduce H^q(L)=0. This proves the global bound for every G.
